findings: Equal-length rc.sysinit data replacement: drops the last two mount echo lines and appends a background Lua start after every mount; only the differing tail is stored.
The ROMFS inode checksum covers the unchanged 32-byte header/name and the filesystem checksum covers its unchanged first 512 bytes.

Physical boot acceptance FAILED on this firmware: on a real Band 11 4.100.179, the /dev/bes_flash writer reported the pin as successful, the band looped from the next boot on, and the user could not recover it (replaced under warranty; reported 2026-11-03, details 2026-11-08; no logs from the band). The success report means the patched tail read back through the driver, and this block holds nothing live besides the ROMFS (below), so the erase gap is the less likely cause; the dangling lua_State (below) restarts the band whether or not the write succeeded. Inferred, not proven. The flash-HAL writer that replaced it is NOT device-tested, so Band 11 builds keep pinned start off except with CANOPUS_BOOT_DEVICE_TEST=1.
The erase block holds only the ROMFS tail (with rcS) and zero padding after it.

MTD up_progmem_eraseblock (0xc330dac) erases inside BASEPRI 0x80, then calls usleep(1) (udelay only in an interrupt or the idle task) before FTL programs the block, so other tasks run while it is blank.

The Supervisor now erases and programs the whole block with the BES flash HAL (symbols flash.app_flash_erase/program/flush) inside one BASEPRI 0x80 section, after a bits-only probe of the dropped echo line; block states are identified by block_crc32; unpinning clears 's' of the hook to '#' without an erase. Emulator evidence only (scripts/emu/boot_smoke.py).

boot.lua runs under the firmware's NSH `lua`, whose luaopen_screen keeps the interpreter's lua_State in a three-slot table (symbol lua.screen_lua_states) for screen_state_cb; only the app framework's lua_module_miwear_close clears a slot, so the state stays there after `lua` exits and every later screen change runs lua_getglobal on freed memory. Same code as 4.100.155 (exact IDB: luaopen_screen 0x0c6d1eb0, screen_state_cb 0x0c6d1dfc, lua_module_miwear_close 0x0c8ea6a0), so the same restart is expected. boot.lua (generated) now clears its own slot, matched against tostring(coroutine.running()), with one aligned `mw` write before anything else.

Mirage q66 4.100.179 (emulator only, 2026-11-08): pinned image, boot.lua without the slot release, a tap at 40 s and every 30 s from 100 s for 300 s: boot.lua ran six times (attempts 1, 2, 3, 1, 1, 2), because starts that reached Manager registration before the fault cleared the counter; another run hung the UI after the first wake (identical screenshots, stopped clock, boot.pending left at 1). The same schedule with the release: one start, the sequence completed, registry.bin written. With boot.pending preset to 3, boot.lua removed /data/canopus/b and returned without loading anything.

Start counter (boot.pending), 2026-11-08: the Supervisor now removes it only once the start has been proven, a minute after the whole sequence and after one screen wake; it used to go as soon as the Manager registered, so a fault that came later restarted the count at every boot. On the fourth start boot.lua removes /data/canopus/b, so later boots run no `lua` at all until the installer's Run writes it again. Emulator evidence only (scripts/emu/boot_smoke.py).
